content:
alice-customer: Hey team — after creating the VPC Endpoint for Redwood PrivateLink, our app started failing to reach the API. We get TLS errors and 502/503 intermittently. No changes on our app side.

maria-support: Sorry you're hitting this, Alice. Can you paste the exact error? Is DNS resolving to the VPC endpoint IPs or public IPs?

alice-customer: Error in logs: "tls: handshake failure: remote error: tls: bad certificate" then upstream 502. Our app resolves api.redwood.example -> 10.12.5.23 (private).

james-eng: Two quick checks: 1) are you using the VPC endpoint private DNS option? 2) do route tables for the affected subnets have routes to the endpoint ENIs?

alice-customer: We didn't explicitly enable private dns when creating the endpoint. We assumed the endpoint would just work. Route tables show no explicit route for the endpoint.

lee-network: If you didn't enable private DNS, your service hostname might still resolve to public IPs depending on resolver. But you said it resolves to 10.12.5.23 which looks like an ENI. Can you share `aws ec2 describe-network-interfaces --filters Name=description,Values=*vpce*` and the subnet IDs for the failing hosts?

alice-customer: pasted outputs (redacted): `eni-0a1b2c3d` in subnet `subnet-0f1e2d3c`, `vpce-0123456789abcdef0` state: Available. Subnet for app is `subnet-0f1e2d3c`.

maria-support: Thanks. Next, please run traceroute (or tcptraceroute) to the endpoint IP from one of the failing hosts and paste. Also try `openssl s_client -connect 10.12.5.23:443 -servername api.redwood.example -showcerts` and paste the first 10 lines.

alice-customer: traceroute to 10.12.5.23 shows 1 hop -> eni in same AZ then * * *. `openssl s_client` shows server certificate CN=*.compute.internal (not our expected cert).

james-eng: That CN is a red flag — looks like traffic is landing on the endpoint ENI but the TLS SNI is not mapped by our side to the public cert. Two likely causes: 1) You're hitting a backend that expects SNI `api.redwood.com` but the SNI sent is `api.redwood.example` (custom domain mismatch), or 2) Traffic is being intercepted by a default listener because routing landed on the wrong target group.

lee-network: Also check security groups on the ENI and customer-side SGs. VPC Endpoint ENIs need their SG to allow inbound 443 from your subnets and ephemeral ports for return. Check NACLs for DENY rules. Run: `aws ec2 describe-network-acls --filters Name=vpc-id,Values=<vpc>`

alice-customer: We had a locked-down NACL and missed ephemeral range 1024-65535. Updated to allow ephemeral and allowed 443 from our app CIDR. Still seeing TLS CN mismatch.

james-eng: OK. Next reproduce steps for us: 1) curl via host in subnet: `curl -v https://api.redwood.example/health` 2) `openssl s_client -connect 10.12.5.23:443 -servername api.redwood.example` 3) `aws ec2 describe-route-tables --filters Name=association.subnet-id,Values=subnet-0f1e2d3c`

alice-customer: curl -v output: `* Connected to 10.12.5.23 (10.12.5.23) port 443` then `* TLS handshake error` followed by `HTTP/1.1 502 Bad Gateway`. Route table shows no VPCE-specific routes.

maria-support: Aha — if route table doesn't have the interface endpoint route entries, packets may hairpin or be SNATed to the NAT/IGW and reach public infra, causing odd TLS certs. Usually AWS creates ENI route entries automatically for interface endpoints when subnets are associated; if you created the endpoint in subnets that aren't associated with the route table, that explains it. Do you use a TGW? Route propagation could be the issue.

alice-customer: We're using a TGW hub. The endpoint subnets are in spoke account, route tables are in spoke, TGW attachments present. Could TGW be dropping endpoint ENI routes?

lee-network: Yes — interface endpoints are regional and tied to VPC ENIs. Traffic over TGW may need specific static routes or route table associations. TGW route propagation doesn't automatically add VPCE interface routes to attached VPCs. You need to ensure the spoke VPCs have routes that point to the ENI or that DNS resolves to IPs reachable over TGW. If you're forcing egress through TGW, return path could be wrong.

james-eng: We suspect split-brain DNS: some hosts resolve to ENI IPs, others to public IPs via corporate resolver. If a host resolves to ENI but traffic egresses via TGW which doesn't have direct path back to the ENI, the source IP might get SNAT and hit a public load balancer with a different cert.

maria-support: Temporary repro test: from the failing host, `curl -v --resolve api.redwood.example:443:10.12.5.23 https://api.redwood.example/health` and compare with `curl -v https://api.redwood.example/health` without --resolve. Also check `nslookup api.redwood.example` and `dig +short` from different subnets.

alice-customer: Done. With --resolve TLS matches correct cert and we get 200. Without --resolve we get the CN mismatch 502. Dig shows inconsistent answers across subnets.

lee-network: That nails DNS inconsistency. Two fixes: enable Private DNS on the VPC endpoint OR configure your DNS forwarder (Route 53 inbound/outbound endpoints or resolver rules) so the service hostname resolves consistently to the endpoint IPs from all subnets.

james-eng: We'll also check on our side that the endpoint service mapping for your account's VPC is configured to honor SNI and map the hostname to the right certificate. I'll escalate to eng-infra to confirm the service-side listener mapping.

deploy-bot: Incident ticket created: RINF-8271, priority P2, assigned to eng-infra. Logs attached: client tls mismatch samples.

maria-support: Alice — steps to resolve on your side: 1) Enable Private DNS for the VPC Endpoint (or add Route53 resolver rules to forward your VPC domain queries to AWS DNS). 2) Ensure TGW route tables include paths for ENI CIDRs or ensure app subnets route directly to local ENI (no SNAT). 3) Confirm SGs and NACLs allow 443 and ephemeral ports. 4) After DNS changes, `dig api.redwood.example` from multiple hosts to confirm consistency.

alice-customer: Enabling Private DNS now, updating resolver rules, and added a static route in TGW for ENI CIDR -> VPC attachment. Will report back in ~15m.

alice-customer (15m later): After enabling Private DNS + TGW route fix everything is green. curl returns 200, `openssl s_client` shows CN=api.redwood.example and cert chain correct. No more 502s.

maria-support: Great! Closing ticket RINF-8271. If anything else pops up, ping us. :thumbsup:

james-eng: We'll follow up with eng-infra to document TGW+VPCE patterns in the KB because this combination seems to trip customers.

alice-customer: Thanks all for the quick help!
